summary.headline: Varroc Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29.9% YoY to INR2,634 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.5% from 9.5% on war-related costs and a tooling sale.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 30% YoY to INR2,634 crore, with India up about 29% and overseas up about 46%. EBITDA margin fell to 8.5% (9.5% a year ago, 9.7% in Q4) on about 0.5% genuine under-recovery of war-related commodity costs, a 0.25% numerator/denominator effect, and about 0.8% from a large low-margin tooling sale (about INR70 crore). PBT before JV and exceptional items was 4.3% of revenue, up 20 bps YoY. Net debt rose to INR527 crore from INR495 crore on front-loaded capex and a INR441 million working-capital build. Management pointed to 20-25% FY27 growth as its ambition, not formal guidance.

segments.name: India operations
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 29% YoY and 10% QoQ, EBITDA up 22% YoY, PBT up 41% YoY; EBITDA margin 10.6% and PBT margin about 7%.

segments.name: Overseas electronics and lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 46% YoY; losses narrowing sequentially. Romania electronics (E/E architecture, passenger vehicle) is now reported separately. Romania targets EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27; 2-wheeler overseas already profitable.

segments.name: E-mobility (EV)
segments.commentary: EV revenue about 16% of total, up 87% YoY. EV powertrain revenue up about 56% YoY versus industry EV volumes up 80-90%; management attributes gap to lower ASPs (high single-digit decline) from product mix, plus early-quarter labour disruption in April-May.

segments.name: ICE powertrain
segments.commentary: Overseas forging is about 3.3% of revenue (per slide 13) and sits in ICE powertrain. Management said about 70% of the business is powertrain-agnostic, with the balance ICE-specific.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of at least 20-25% seen as an ambition, not guidance; mid-to-high teens was guided earlier.

Around 50 bps of war-related under-recovery expected to be recovered from customers mostly in Q1-Q2; inflation recovery is arithmetic and may take 1-2 quarters. Most other one-time impacts (tooling) not expected to repeat to this extent in Q2.
Long-term target of 10% PBT in 3-4 years; management said medium term 'soon' and declined to give a year-end PBT number.
FY27 capex of INR500-550 crore (India plus overseas), heavier than the last 2-3 years, mainly e-mobility capacity.
Overseas revenue expected to roughly double YoY this year (electronics and lighting); overseas PBT target 10% in 3-4 years.
Revenue ambition: roughly double to INR20,000 crore by FY31 from about INR10,000 crore this year, ~20% overseas, ~10% from inorganic routes.
Zero-debt target for FY28 retained, though management said it will pursue it sooner if possible.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR160 crore, mostly capacity additions; the net debt increase was partly working capital.
FY27 capex INR500-550 crore including overseas, with e-mobility capacity and capacity to service EV models with engine-agnostic products the main drivers.
Traction motor business: one non-Bajaj win to start SOP in Q2 FY27; two further customers in advanced discussions with SOPs expected within FY27.
Eric Hammond appointed CTO for Business Unit I (25 years global automotive technology leadership in electrification, software-defined vehicles, functional safety).
demand_pricing: Net new business wins of about INR600 crore annual peak revenue; about two-thirds e-mobility volume expansion on existing programs, balance mainly a 4-wheeler lighting win for Thailand and smaller wins.
Bajaj share of annual peak revenue in the order book at 75% vs 58% of order-book count (as stated by CFO); management says non-Bajaj wins are growing.
Pricing: management expects no double-digit ASP declines; OEMs are cost-optimised, and component integration into smaller boxes may raise ASP.
PBT margins of ICE and EV are expected to be broadly comparable at PBT level; EBITDA is not a like-for-like metric across product lines given capital intensity.

qa_highlights.question: Split of the ~INR600 crore Q1 order win between e-mobility and 4-wheeler lighting?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Jain said about two-thirds is e-mobility volume expansion on existing programs; the balance is mainly a 4-wheeler lighting win (Thailand) plus smaller wins.

qa_highlights.question: Margin recovery of the ~50 bps war-related under-recovery and full-year margin view?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahendra Kumar said recovery efforts are underway, with most expected between Q1 and Q2; the inflation element is arithmetic and may take 1-2 quarters, while one-time tooling impacts should not repeat to this extent in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 growth expectation after 30% Q1 growth versus earlier mid-to-high teens guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Tarang Jain said at least 20-25% growth looks achievable for FY27; Mahendra Kumar clarified this is an ambition, not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: EV powertrain revenue up about 56% vs industry EV volumes up 80-90%: what is the ASP decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Jain estimated a high single-digit ASP decline driven by product mix, and said April-May labour disruption, now recovered, also weighed on the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Overseas breakeven timing and steady-state margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahendra Kumar said 2-wheeler overseas is already profitable, Romania targets EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27, and the long-term goal is 10% PBT in 3-4 years; Dhruv Jain said overseas revenue can roughly double this year.

qa_highlights.question: Capex quantum and working-capital drivers of the net debt increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahendra Kumar said FY27 capex will be INR500-550 crore including overseas; Q1 capex was about INR160 crore, and the INR316 million net debt rise was partly due to a INR441 million working-capital build from inventory and pending war-related recoveries.

qa_highlights.question: Is ~INR20,000 crore FY31 revenue organic, and what is the overseas share?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahendra Kumar said about 10% would come from inorganic routes and possibly some non-auto; about 20% would be overseas and 80% India.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA is not like-for-like; can ICE and EV margins converge at PBT level?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Jain said EBITDA is distorted by capital intensity across product lines, and that ICE and EV PBT margins should be broadly comparable.

risks_watch: Recovery of the ~50 bps war-related commodity under-recovery from customers in Q1-Q2; management says inflation recovery is arithmetic and may take 1-2 quarters.
EV ASP erosion: EV powertrain revenue up about 56% vs industry EV volumes up 80-90%, with high single-digit ASP decline; management says no double-digit ASP cuts expected.
Net debt rising to INR527 crore and working capital build; zero-debt target for FY28 retained but timing uncertain.
Romania electronics EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27 is a key test; overseas launch timing questioned by analysts.
Customer concentration: Bajaj at 75% of annual peak revenue in the order book versus 58% of order-book count; non-Bajaj wins not quantified.

Capex of INR500-550 crore is heavier than prior years; execution and return on EV capacity to monitor. Also watch for tooling-sale-driven margin volatility and whether a non-Bajaj traction motor SOP starts in Q2 FY27.
key_quotes: Coming to PBT during Q1, it was at 4.3% versus 4.1% shown last year.
We don't take it as a guidance, but it's more like our ambition.
I wouldn't expect double-digit changes in ASPs that will take place.
So we are not changing our message from the past.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and EV demand, with a clear FY27 20-25% growth ambition. Cautious and deliberately non-committal on quantified guidance: repeatedly declined year-end PBT, customer-level forecasts, and new customer names, and framed the 20-25% growth and 10% PBT target as ambition or medium term.

adds.what: FY27 capex of INR500-550 crore (India plus overseas), mainly e-mobility capacity; Q1 FY27 capex about INR160 crore, mostly capacity additions
Traction motor business: one non-Bajaj customer win to start SOP in Q2 FY27
Two further traction motor customers in advanced discussions, SOPs expected within FY27
Romania electronics unit targets EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27 (not a capacity addition)

growth.why: Q1 revenue up 29.9% YoY to INR2,634 crore with India +29% and overseas +46%, net new wins ~INR600 crore annual peak revenue, and FY27 capex of INR500-550 crore for e-mobility; but the 20-25% FY27 growth is management ambition rather than formal guidance, and utilisation was not stated.
